evidence.detail: HEAD exactly matches the launcher-supplied target SHA; the supplied base object resolves exactly. The reviewed diff changes seven allowed files and contains no product-source changes.

The workflow retains the three Python checks and adds SHA-pinned actions/setup-node, Node 22, npm caching keyed to frontend/package-lock.json, then npm ci, npm run build, and npm test in frontend/ on push and pull_request.
git diff --check completed successfully with no whitespace errors.

The committed issue record reports round-0 results of 188 backend tests, successful compile/governance/build, 91 frontend tests, and a negative-test fallback producing exit 1. These are durable author-provided records, but raw command output is not included in this candidate.

Independent backend execution discovered all 188 tests but ended with 76 errors because the read-only sandbox prohibits loopback socket binding; the errors were PermissionError from ThreadingHTTPServer.bind, not assertion failures.
Independent governance validation could not complete because the read-only sandbox provides no writable temporary directory.
Independent frontend tests could not start because node_modules is absent and vitest is unavailable. npm ci could not be run because installation is a protected action and the checkout is read-only.

evidence: Expected: project/status/CURRENT.md must consistently identify the current gate, repair round, reviewed candidate, and next permitted action from repository files alone.

Observed: the Stage row says ISSUE_REPAIR and round 1 is in progress, while Active issue says REVIEWING, round 0; Issue repair round says none is open; Latest Codex issue review omits ISSUE-0014; Tracked follow-up calls the candidate under round-0 review/repair; and Next required actor/Next permitted action instruct launching a review against the round-0 candidate.

The issue record independently identifies status REPAIRING and identifies d72dbd9a5481ec8dc69143fb31aef7a15fc0445b as the round-1 candidate, confirming the CURRENT.md rows are stale rather than an alternative valid state.
This is the same class of governance inconsistency round 1 was intended to repair, so a fresh task still cannot reconstruct one authoritative current state as AGENTS.md requires.
findings.remediation: Synchronize every CURRENT.md status row to ISSUE-0014 round 1 at d72dbd9a5481ec8dc69143fb31aef7a15fc0445b: use REPAIRING/ISSUE_REPAIR consistently, state that repair round 1 is open, make ISSUE-0014 round 0 the latest recorded Codex issue review, and identify the next action as a fresh round-1 review of the exact current candidate. Recheck the whole table for stale round-0 wording.
findings.title: Round-1 status record still directs the workflow to round 0
findings.verification: From a fresh checkout, compare the claudex-state block, Stage, Active issue, Issue repair round, Latest Codex issue review, Open blockers, Tracked follow-up, Next required actor, and Next permitted action rows with project/issues/ISSUE-0014.md; all must consistently identify round 1 and the exact candidate being reviewed. Then run python3 scripts/validate_repo.py in an environment with a writable temporary directory.

limitations: The checkout is read-only, so npm ci, npm run build, py_compile, and the negative-test mutation could not be independently executed.
Frontend dependencies are absent; npm test failed before test execution because vitest was not installed.
The sandbox denies loopback socket binding, causing 76 of 188 backend tests to error; therefore the claimed passing backend result could not be independently confirmed.
The sandbox has no writable temporary directory, so governance validation could not complete.

No local GitHub Actions runner or hosted workflow result was available. The committed negative-CI evidence exercises the composed npm commands, not YAML parsing or hosted-runner failure propagation; DECISION-029 explicitly accepts that limitation.

The isolated checkout is grafted and does not contain the referenced round-0 commit object c4cb4d28f9b710e4f24366ec6fbb61e810246d96, although its committed review report is present, so that intermediate commit could not be independently inspected.
review.summary: BLOCKED. The CI workflow change is scoped and structurally satisfies the requested Node setup and npm command ordering, but the round-1 governance repair remains internally contradictory and still directs the next actor to review round 0. Independent required checks also could not be completed in the read-only, no-network, no-loopback sandbox, so PASS is prohibited. Residual risks are the accepted lack of workflow-runner-level negative proof and ordinary npm build-time supply-chain exposure recorded under RISK-009.
